headline: Two of your senior people disagree on direction
body: They want to take the product in opposite directions, and neither will budge. One of them has started talking about leaving.

options.label: Back one of them and move on
options.detail: Pick a side, commit publicly, and accept that the other one may not stay.
options.storyHeadline: Picked a side in a team conflict

options.label: Find a middle ground
options.detail: Build a hybrid neither of them fully wanted, so both stay unhappy but neither leaves.
options.storyHeadline: Navigated conflicting visions

headline: You're burning out
body: You haven't slept properly in weeks and your team can tell. One engineer just quit, and cited it as part of why.

options.label: Take a real vacation
options.detail: A full week off, no laptop, no email — actually disconnect.
options.storyHeadline: Took a real break to recharge

options.label: Push through it
options.detail: Too much is happening right now to stop. Keep going.
options.storyHeadline: Burned out but kept going

headline: A star operator wants to join
body: Someone with a proven track record of building and scaling companies wants in — a real adult in the room, if you can afford them.

options.label: Hire them as COO, right away
options.detail: A real salary and a clean 10% equity stake, starting Monday.
options.storyHeadline: Hired an experienced operator as COO

options.label: Bring them on as an advisor first
options.detail: No equity yet — a lighter arrangement to see how it works before committing.
options.storyHeadline: Got experienced advisor

headline: The co-founder wants out
body: {COFOUNDER} has been quiet for months. Today they said they're done. They hold their stake, and they're keeping it — unless you do something about it.

options.label: Buy the shares back
options.detail: It costs you, but the company is fully yours again.
options.storyHeadline: Bought out a departing co-founder
options.mentorHint: The company's fully yours again. So is everything that goes wrong from here.

options.label: Let them walk with it
options.detail: They go, and they keep every point. The story writes itself.
options.storyHeadline: Let a co-founder walk with their stake
options.mentorHint: They keep every point. You'll see their name on the cap table at every future raise.

options.label: Ask for six more months
options.detail: A real gamble on whether that helps.
options.storyHeadline: Asked a burned-out co-founder for six more months

gamble.loseText: They left anyway, and took two engineers with them.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The co-founder left, and took people with them

headline: Someone is stealing
body: Your bookkeeper has been moving small amounts for two years. It adds up to more than a year of your own salary.

options.label: Police
options.detail: Legal fees. It goes public.
options.storyHeadline: Went to the police over embezzlement

options.label: Quiet settlement
options.detail: Cheaper. Nobody finds out.
options.storyHeadline: Settled an embezzlement quietly

options.label: Let it go
options.detail: The rest of the team eventually works it out.
options.storyHeadline: Let an embezzlement slide

headline: The star hire is poison
body: Your best salesperson brings in a third of the revenue and has made four people cry this year.

options.label: Fire them
options.detail: Revenue drops. The team recovers.
options.storyHeadline: Fired a brilliant, toxic hire

options.label: Keep them
options.detail: Revenue holds. Two good people leave.
options.storyHeadline: Kept a toxic top performer

headline: Everyone wants to work from home forever
body: The office is empty on Fridays. Then Thursdays.

options.label: Close the office
options.detail: Cash lasts longer. Morale is up. New hires ramp slower.
options.storyHeadline: Closed the office for good

options.label: Order everyone back
options.detail: Morale drops. Four people quit. Output rises.
options.storyHeadline: Ordered everyone back to the office

options.label: Let each team decide
options.detail: Nothing dramatic. Which is its own outcome.
options.storyHeadline: Let teams decide their own working pattern

headline: The first firing
body: Someone isn't working out. Everyone knows. You've been avoiding it for four months.

options.label: Do it today
options.detail: The team was waiting for this.
options.storyHeadline: Finally made the first firing

options.label: Give them another quarter
options.detail: The problem grows.
options.storyHeadline: Gave an underperformer another quarter

headline: Nobody knows what the company does
body: You asked six employees to describe the product. You got six answers.

options.label: Cut half the product
options.detail: Revenue dips now, doubles down later.
options.storyHeadline: Cut half the product to clarify the story

options.label: Hire someone to fix the messaging
options.detail: It costs, and it works.
options.storyHeadline: Hired to fix a confused message

options.label: Ignore it
options.detail: Nothing, until the next event.
options.storyHeadline: Ignored the messaging problem

headline: Half the team wants to fire you
body: Three senior people went to the board without telling you.

options.label: Fight it
options.detail: A real fight for control of your own company.
options.storyHeadline: Fought to keep control of the company

gamble.winText: You kept it, and your authority with it.
gamble.loseText: You're out. You keep your shares, not your seat.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost the fight for the company

options.label: Bring in a professional boss and stay as founder
options.detail: You keep every share. You lose the wheel.
options.storyHeadline: Brought in a CEO and stepped back

headline: You disagree about direction
body: {COFOUNDER} wants one thing, you want the other. Both are defensible.

options.label: Insist
options.detail: You get your way. Something between you is different afterwards.
options.storyHeadline: Insisted on your own direction over a co-founder

options.label: Give in
options.detail: They're energised. It might even be the right call.
options.storyHeadline: Gave way to a co-founder's direction

gamble.loseText: They weren't, but at least morale held.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Gave way to a co-founder's direction

options.label: Split the effort
options.detail: Neither happens properly.
options.storyHeadline: Split the effort between two directions

headline: They're working less than you
body: Same shares, different hours. You've noticed. They know you've noticed.

options.label: Say it directly
options.detail: Uncomfortable, resolved.
options.storyHeadline: Said it directly to a co-founder

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: It compounds for three years, then ends badly.
options.storyHeadline: Said nothing about an uneven co-founder split

options.label: Renegotiate the shares
options.detail: A real gamble on whether that clears the air.
options.storyHeadline: Tried to renegotiate a co-founder's shares

gamble.loseStoryHeadline: A co-founder left over renegotiated shares

headline: Their friend needs a job
body: You don't rate the candidate. {COFOUNDER} feels strongly.

options.label: Hire them
options.detail: A mediocre hire. {COFOUNDER} owes you one.
options.storyHeadline: Hired a co-founder's friend

options.label: Block it
options.detail: You're right. They resent it for a year.
options.storyHeadline: Blocked a co-founder's friend-hire

headline: Who is actually in charge
body: The team asks two people and gets two answers.

options.label: Split responsibilities formally
options.detail: Clear, slightly cold, works.
options.storyHeadline: Formally split responsibilities with a co-founder
options.mentorHint: Clean on paper. Every decision at the boundary between you two now takes a meeting.

options.label: One of you is the boss
options.detail: Morale improves. One of you is unhappy forever.
options.storyHeadline: Settled who was actually the boss
options.mentorHint: Morale goes up. It goes up for one of you, and stays up for as long as the other one lets it.

options.label: Leave it
options.detail: Decisions take twice as long, permanently.
options.storyHeadline: Left it unresolved who was in charge
options.mentorHint: Nothing happens today. Every decision after this one happens slightly slower, for as long as you both run this.

headline: They got a better offer
body: A large company offered {COFOUNDER} a salary you cannot match.

options.label: More shares to stay
options.detail: It costs you equity, not cash.
options.storyHeadline: Gave a co-founder more shares to stay
options.mentorHint: It costs equity, not cash — the kind of cost that's easy to agree to and hard to get back.

options.label: Let them go with their shares
options.detail: They keep every point. It's awkward forever.
options.storyHeadline: Let a co-founder go to a better offer
options.mentorHint: They keep every point, and you keep explaining to investors why they're not on the team anymore.

options.label: Buy them out
options.detail: Clean, and expensive.
options.storyHeadline: Bought out a co-founder before they left
options.mentorHint: Clean, and expensive. You're paying today for a decision you can't actually undo.

headline: Your investor wants weekly updates
body: They mean well. It's four hours a week.

options.label: Do it properly
options.detail: Four hours a week, forever.
options.storyHeadline: Started sending proper weekly updates

options.label: Monthly only
options.detail: They're mildly annoyed. You get your time back.
options.storyHeadline: Cut investor updates back to monthly

headline: The board wants a bigger plan
body: They think you're not ambitious enough.

options.label: Give them the aggressive plan
options.detail: Cash lasts less time. Revenue can climb fast.
options.storyHeadline: Committed to the board's aggressive plan

options.label: Give them the honest plan
options.detail: They're disappointed. You hit it.
options.storyHeadline: Gave the board an honest, smaller plan

headline: An investor wants out
body: They need to return money to their own backers and want to sell their shares.

options.label: Buy them out yourself
options.detail: Costs, but you get the shares.
options.storyHeadline: Bought out a departing investor
options.mentorHint: The cash leaves today. The shares you bought back should be growing, not sitting on your balance sheet.

options.label: Nothing you can do
options.detail: They push for a sale of the whole company from now on.
options.storyHeadline: Let a restless investor stay on the cap table
options.mentorHint: It costs nothing right now. What it costs is a cap table with someone on it who wants out and can't leave.

headline: They ask you to cut staff
body: The board wants a 20% reduction. You think it's premature.

options.label: Do it
options.detail: Cash lasts longer. Morale drops hard.
options.storyHeadline: Cut staff at the board's request

options.label: Refuse and hit the numbers instead
options.detail: A real bet on proving the board wrong.
options.storyHeadline: Refused a board-mandated cut

gamble.winText: You hit the numbers. The board backed off.
gamble.loseText: You cut deeper, six months later, on worse terms.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Proved the board wrong on cuts
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Cut deeper than the board first asked

headline: You never registered the name properly
body: Someone else just did.

options.label: Buy it from them
options.detail: A clean, annoying payment.
options.storyHeadline: Bought back your own company name
options.mentorHint: A clean, annoying payment. Whoever registered it now knows exactly how much your name is worth to you.

options.label: Change the name
options.detail: Expensive. A clean slate.
options.storyHeadline: Changed the company name entirely
options.mentorHint: Expensive. Every customer who already knows you by the old name has to learn the new one.

headline: Staff shares were never formalised
body: You promised people shares. Nothing was signed.

options.label: Sort it out properly
options.detail: Morale climbs. Everyone is finally clear.
options.storyHeadline: Formalised staff equity properly

options.label: Keep promising
options.detail: Morale collapses the moment anyone asks a lawyer.
options.storyHeadline: Kept promising staff equity informally

headline: Someone claims you copied them
body: A letter from a company you've never heard of.

options.label: Fight it
options.detail: Expensive, and you'll probably win.
options.storyHeadline: Fought an accusation of copying

gamble.loseText: You lost, and paid for it.

options.label: Settle quietly
options.detail: Done, at a price.
options.storyHeadline: Settled a copying dispute quietly

headline: What are you actually for?
body: You're doing a bit of everything and none of it well.

options.label: Only do sales
options.detail: Revenue climbs. The product drifts.
options.storyHeadline: Focused entirely on sales

options.label: Only do product
options.detail: The product improves. Revenue is flat.
options.storyHeadline: Focused entirely on product

options.label: Only manage people
options.detail: Morale climbs. You stop enjoying it.
options.storyHeadline: Became a full-time manager

headline: Someone offers you a job
body: A big salary, no risk, starts Monday.

options.label: Stay
options.detail: You'll think about this again someday.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down a safe job to stay

headline: You're bored
body: It works. It runs. You're not needed the way you were.

options.label: Start something new inside the company
options.detail: A real risk to something that already works.
options.storyHeadline: Started something new inside a stable company

gamble.winText: It revived you, and the numbers.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: A new bet inside the company paid off
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: A new bet inside the company backfired

options.label: Hire someone to run it and step back
options.detail: You keep your shares. You keep your evenings.
options.storyHeadline: Hired a CEO and stepped back

headline: Your first employee wants to buy the company
body: They've been there since the start and they've found the money.

options.label: Sell to them
options.detail: Take their offer, at whatever the market says the company is worth.
options.storyHeadline: Sold the company to the person who joined second
options.mentorHint: What you're actually choosing here is the ending you get to tell, not the number on the cheque.

options.label: Turn them down, hold out for a bigger buyer
options.detail: Keep running the company and wait for a better offer to come along instead.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down the first employee to hold out for more
options.mentorHint: You might get a bigger number later. The person who believed in this before anyone else doesn't get to be part of it either way.

headline: Give shares to the staff
body: You could give away a slice to everyone who works there.

options.label: Give away 10% to everyone
options.detail: Nobody leaves for a decade.
options.storyHeadline: Gave staff a real stake in the company

options.label: Keep it
options.detail: Richer. Lonelier.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the equity for yourself

headline: What do you actually stand for?
body: Someone asked and you didn't have an answer.

options.label: Write it down with the team
options.detail: Two days. Occasionally useful.
options.storyHeadline: Wrote the company's values with the team

options.label: Nothing
options.detail: Fine, until you need it.
options.storyHeadline: Never wrote down what the company stands for

headline: The team wants to know what everyone earns
body: A group of them raised it at the last all-hands: full salary transparency, company-wide. They're waiting on an answer.

options.label: Publish everything
options.detail: Three difficult months. Permanent trust after.
options.storyHeadline: Made every salary public

options.label: Publish bands only
options.detail: The middle path. Works.
options.storyHeadline: Published salary bands, not figures

options.label: Refuse
options.detail: Morale drops.
options.storyHeadline: Refused salary transparency

headline: They want to bring in a third
body: {COFOUNDER} found someone excellent, who wants founder-level shares to join.

options.label: Agree
options.detail: A real third founder, with real equity.
options.storyHeadline: Brought on a third co-founder
options.mentorHint: Real equity, permanently split three ways. That's true in the good years and the bad ones.

options.label: Employee terms instead
options.detail: A smaller stake, if they'll even take it.
options.storyHeadline: Offered employee terms instead of a third founder

gamble.winStoryHeadline: A senior hire joined on employee terms
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: A senior hire declined employee terms

options.label: No third founder
options.detail: {COFOUNDER} is quietly disappointed.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down a third co-founder
options.mentorHint: Nothing costs money today. Someone excellent is now available to a competitor instead.

headline: They got famous
body: {COFOUNDER} posted something unrelated to work. Nine million views.

options.label: Put them in front of every camera
options.detail: Signups spike. They stop working.
options.storyHeadline: Put a newly-famous co-founder in front of every camera

options.label: Ask them to keep it separate
options.detail: They're not thrilled about it.
options.storyHeadline: Asked a famous co-founder to keep it separate

options.label: Nothing
options.detail: It might just fade.
options.storyHeadline: Let a co-founder's fame run its course

gamble.loseText: They left to do it full-time.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: A co-founder's fame faded on its own
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: A co-founder left to chase their fame full-time

headline: It's the thing about them again
body: {COFOUNDER} {COFOUNDER_TRAIT} — and this week it's a real problem, not a quirk.

options.label: Address it directly
options.detail: An honest conversation, and some cleanup.
options.storyHeadline: Addressed a co-founder's pattern head-on

options.label: Let it go
options.detail: Easier this week. Not next week.
options.storyHeadline: Let a co-founder's pattern slide again

headline: Someone excellent wants in
body: You've done everything alone. Someone excellent wants to join, at real equity.

options.label: Take them on
options.detail: A real partner, and a real stake.
options.storyHeadline: Took on a co-founder after years solo
options.mentorHint: A real stake, forever. You've just given up the thing that made every decision only yours to make.

options.label: Hire them instead
options.detail: A smaller stake, and you stay in charge.
options.storyHeadline: Hired a would-be co-founder as an employee instead
options.mentorHint: A smaller stake, and you stay in charge — of someone who could have been an equal.

options.label: Stay solo
options.detail: Nothing changes, and it stays hard.
options.storyHeadline: Stayed solo rather than take on a partner
options.mentorHint: Nothing changes. It also doesn't get easier, and the someone-excellent doesn't wait.
